summary: The daily answers check now also compares the verdicts members serve. The summary carries a reader, reader/slots/verdicts, with one key per answer whose claim this member judges invalid, so a claim one member serves as verified and another as invalid opens an answers-disagreement fault naming the claim and reason.

replay.detail: Verdicts are read, not changed; the summary is local and recomputed each check.

schema.detail: No table or column change. The kept summary file beside the store gains the reader's keys; a build change recomputes it as before.

compatibility.detail: The reader is one more summary kind. Two members compare it only when both carry it, in this release and in every earlier one: earlier builds compare a reader/slots/ kind only when both summaries carry it. A member sends it only beside fold readers, as every daemon runs them, so an earlier build never takes it as a sign that the peer runs fold readers it lacks. A mixed fleet raises no fault in either direction. Tested against the previous release's comparison rules.

downtime.detail: None. The summary pass reads the claims still to be judged and the verdicts other than verified and unsigned once, then looks each answer up in them. Measured on a copy of a real member (1.1 million answer keys), the pass took the same time with the reader as without it, within 1.2% either way over two rounds. A member mid-requeue leaves the reader out until the requeue finishes.

manual.detail: Nothing to do. An answers-disagreement fault for reader/slots/verdicts names each claim and the verdict and reason the member serves. Two members that judge one claim differently have found a bug in judging or in what it read; keep both stores for the investigation.

recovery.detail: Roll back to the previous release: its summary has no verdict reader and its peers compare nothing for it.
